statement: Target population and observed sample must not collapse.
Sampling frame coverage and target-population membership must not collapse.
Observational unit and storage row must not collapse.
Selection design and analysis procedure must not collapse.
Estimand, estimator and realized estimate must remain distinct.
An estimate is not the unknown population truth.
Standard error is estimator uncertainty under a design/model, not raw-data spread.
Confidence and credible intervals have different probability semantics.
Prediction intervals and parameter confidence intervals target different objects.
Measurement uncertainty and sampling uncertainty must not collapse.
Missing, null, structural absence, censored and numerical zero must not collapse.
MCAR, MAR or MNAR is not directly observed from a missing-value pattern.
Survey/design weight is not automatically a frequency, importance or loss weight.
Describing the captured data occurrence is not inference to a population.
Exploratory discovery and confirmatory error-controlled analysis must not collapse.
Association or regression coefficient is not a causal effect without identification.
Numerical convergence or fit completion is not model adequacy.
Passing selected diagnostics does not prove a model true or fit for every use.
A p-value is not the posterior probability that the null hypothesis is true.
A p-value is not effect size or practical importance.
Statistical significance is not an operational or policy authorization.
Failure to reject is not evidence of equivalence or no effect.
A nominal error rate is not the realized false-discovery proportion.
Family-wise error rate and false-discovery rate must not collapse.
A multiplicity family is a semantic claim family, not merely every p-value in one file.
Bootstrap does not universally mean resampling independent rows.
Equal seed alone does not establish reproducibility across algorithms, versions or execution orders.
Robustness to perturbation and computational reproducibility must not collapse.
Re-execution on the same inputs and replication with new data must not collapse.
Replication in another study and generalization to a target context must not collapse.
Sensitivity analysis of assumptions and supplementary analysis of another question must not collapse.
A posterior distribution is conditional on model, prior, data and computation, not a truth distribution.
A finite MCMC sample is not the posterior distribution.
An acceptable convergence diagnostic does not prove correct implementation or model adequacy.
Common/fixed-effect and random-effects meta-analysis target different models.
Between-study heterogeneity is not automatically sampling noise.
Numerically convertible effect estimates are not automatically semantically poolable.
An analytical finding is not a relying-party decision or effect authorization.
Statistical evidence and acceptance under a policy must not collapse.
Notebook cell order is not necessarily execution order.
Stored notebook output is not proof that the recorded source/environment reproduces it.
A provider API, default or successful return does not own statistical meaning.
Methods in the same catalog category are not interchangeable without equal assumptions, target and guarantees.
Statistical uncertainty and decision loss/risk must not collapse.
Nominal coverage under a model is not fitness for a domain decision.
An AI or agent may propose an analysis but cannot infer missing design facts, waive diagnostics or authorize a claim/effect.
